subtitle: When Empires Fall, Words Rise: Sarala Das and the Odia Mahabharata

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Sarala Das seated under a village tree, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, distant outline of Puri and a fading royal banner on the horizon
panels.action: Sarala Das sits cross-legged beneath a broad tree, palm-leaf in hand, as a worn royal pennant droops over a faraway fort and the spires of Jagannath’s temple glow in the evening haze.

dialogue.text: As the Ganga kings fade and the Gajapati sun rises, Sarala Das turns the Sanskrit Mahabharata into Odia, giving common people an epic voice that outlives the throne.

i18n.hi: गंगा राजा ढलते हैं, गजपति सूरज उगता है, सरला दास संस्कृत महाभारत को ओड़िया में गढ़ते हैं, आम लोगों को सिंहासन से लंबी चलने वाली महाकाव्य आवाज़ देते हैं।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye view over coastal Odisha, with the Konark Sun Temple and Jagannath Temple standing against the sea
panels.action: An expansive coastal Odisha landscape stretches from Konark’s stone wheels to Jagannath’s towering temple at Puri, fishing boats bobbing on the Bay of Bengal under heavy clouds.

dialogue.text: For two centuries the Eastern Ganga kings ruled this coast, raising Jagannath’s temple at Puri and the stone chariot of the Sun at Konark, binding land and sea in ritual and revenue.

i18n.hi: दो सौ साल तक पूर्वी गंगा राजा इस तट पर राज करते रहे, पुरी में जगन्नाथ मंदिर और कोणार्क में सूर्य का पत्थर रथ खड़ा किया, ज़मीन और समंदर को कर्मकांड और करों से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a royal hall in decline, with a solitary throne and neglected regalia
panels.action: Inside a dim palace hall, an ornate throne stands empty; dusty ceremonial umbrellas lean against cracked pillars, as two nervous courtiers whisper at the far end.

dialogue.text: By the mid-fifteenth century, Bhanu Deva IV’s Eastern Ganga line had grown weak; ministers and commanders held the power, while the king’s authority thinned behind palace walls.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के बीच तक भानु देव चौथे की पूर्वी गंगा वंश कमज़ोर पड़ गई; ताकत मंत्रियों और सेनापतियों के हाथ में, राजा की सत्ता महल की दीवारों के पीछे पतली हो गई।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a military camp under new banners near Cuttack, showing disciplined troops and scribes
panels.action: In a sprawling camp near Cuttack, rows of armoured soldiers stand in formation beneath fresh sun-emblazoned standards, while temple-bred scribes sit at low desks, scratching records on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: From this fragile court emerged Kapilendra Deva, a powerful commander who seized the throne around 1434–35 and founded the Suryavamsha Gajapati line, claiming the radiance of the Sun.

i18n.hi: इसी नाज़ुक दरबार से एक ताकतवर सेनापति निकले—कपिलेंद्र देव, जिन्होंने 1434–35 के आसपास राजगद्दी छीनी, सूर्यवंश गजपति वंश की नींव रखी, खुद को सूर्य की आभा से जोड़ा।

panels.shot: close-up of a stone inscription being carved, chisels striking under supervision
panels.action: A sculptor leans over a stone slab, carefully chipping Odia and Sanskrit letters as a priestly supervisor watches, rolled-up plans of the inscription resting by his feet.

dialogue.text: Kapilendra’s own inscriptions at Gopinathpur and Jagannath’s temple list conquests and gifts. They show a ruler stitching territory and devotion together with words carved in stone.

i18n.hi: गोपीनाथपुर और जगन्नाथ मंदिर में कपिलेंद्र की खुद की शिलालेख जीतों और दानों की सूची हैं। वे दिखाते हैं कैसे शासक ने पत्थर पर लिखे शब्दों से इलाकों और भक्तिभाव को सिल दिया।

panels.shot: quiet medium shot in a rural setting near Jagatsinghpur, focusing on Sarala Das as a working man amid fields and trees
panels.action: In a village near Jagatsinghpur, Sarala Das, sturdy and simple in dress, walks a narrow path between green fields and toddy palms, a small bundle of palm leaves tucked under his arm.

dialogue.text: In this world of kings and temple records lived Sarala Das, remembered as Siddheswara Parida, a man of the countryside whose name would become the first great pillar of Odia literature.

i18n.hi: राजाओं और मंदिर दर्जों की इसी दुनिया में सरला दास रहते थे, जिन्हें सिद्धेश्वर परिडा कहा जाता है—गाँव-देहात का आदमी, जिसका नाम ओड़िया साहित्य का पहला बड़ा स्तंभ बना।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a modest village house with Sarala Das watching Brahmin scholars recite
panels.action: Inside a humble courtyard house, a few Brahmin scholars sit by oil lamps reciting Sanskrit verses, while Sarala Das stands just outside the circle, listening intently, fingers tracing lines on a plain palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Sanskrit learning thrived in royal and temple circles, but most villagers only heard its music from a distance. Sarala listened, absorbed stories, and felt their weight in everyday speech.

i18n.hi: संस्कृत विद्या राजदरबारों और मंदिर मंडलियों में खिल रही थी, पर ज़्यादातर गाँव वाले उसकी धुन दूर से ही सुनते थे। सरला सुनते रहे, कहानियाँ सोखते रहे, और उनके भार को रोज़ की बोलचाल में महसूस किया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sarala Das under a tree, surrounded by attentive villagers
panels.action: Under the shade of the same village tree, Sarala Das sits surrounded by farmers, fisherfolk, and women with water pots, his hand raised mid-story as they lean in, eyes fixed on him.

dialogue.speaker: sarala_das
dialogue.text: If Bhima lifts a mace, you must feel it in your own hands.

i18n.hi: जब भीम गदा उठाए, तुम्हें इसका भार अपने हाथों में महसूस होना चाहिए।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Sarala Das beginning to write on palm leaves by lamplight
panels.action: By a single flickering lamp, Sarala Das sits cross-legged, a sharp stylus poised over a fresh palm leaf, earlier leaves piled neatly beside him, his brow furrowed in concentrated resolve.

dialogue.text: Somewhere in the 15th century, in Kapilendra’s time, he began a vast labor: to tell the Mahabharata anew, not as a strict Sanskrit copy, but as an Odia epic in the people’s tongue.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी में कहीं, कपिलेंद्र के समय, उन्होंने एक विराट काम शुरू किया: महाभारत को फिर से कहना—सख्त संस्कृत नकल नहीं, बल्कि लोगों की भाषा में ओड़िया महाकाव्य।

panels.shot: close-up on the first leaf with invocation, Sarala Das writing a royal and divine invocation
panels.action: A close view shows Sarala Das’s hand inscribing an invocation on a palm leaf, with faintly visible words naming Kapilendra Deva and deities as the stylus presses careful grooves.

dialogue.text: In his Sarala Mahabharata he invokes Kapilendra Deva and divine powers, tying his work to the Gajapati court and Jagannath’s sacred world, yet directing his words toward ordinary hearers.

i18n.hi: अपनी सरला महाभारत में वह कपिलेंद्र देव और देवी शक्तियों का आह्वान करते हैं, अपने काम को गजपति दरबार और जगन्नाथ की पवित्र दुनिया से जोड़ते हुए, पर शब्द साधारण सुनने वालों की ओर मोड़ देते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic montage-style wide shot showing imagined Mahabharata scenes emerging around Sarala Das
panels.action: Sarala Das writes at the center while around him faint, non-violent visions of warriors, forests, chariots, and village scenes swirl in the air, blending Kurukshetra with Odishan rivers and groves.

dialogue.text: He did not simply translate. He reshaped episodes, wove local memories, used meters that matched village songs, building a Mahabharata that felt at once ancient and deeply Odia.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने सिर्फ अनुवाद नहीं किया। प्रसंग बदले, लोक-स्मृतियाँ पिरोईं, गाँव के गीतों से मिलते छंद चुने, एक ऐसी महाभारत रची जो एक साथ पुरानी भी लगे और गहरे ओड़िया भी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sarala Das reciting to a small gathering, with gestures and vivid expression
panels.action: In the village square, Sarala Das stands and recites from a palm leaf, his voice strong, arms drawing arcs in the air, as his listeners silently follow every turn of the story.

dialogue.text: Verses of warriors, queens, and vows now moved in spoken Odia. When he recited, people heard the fate of kings in the rhythm of their own daily speech and songs.

i18n.hi: योद्धाओं, रानियों और प्रतिज्ञाओं के पद अब बोले जाने वाले ओड़िया में चल पड़े। जब वह सुनाते, लोग राजाओं की तकदीर को अपनी रोज़ की बोली और गीतों की लय में सुनते।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot as a temple scribe listens, hinting at manuscript circulation
panels.action: At the edge of the gathering, a temple scribe with a cloth bag of palm leaves listens keenly, eyes narrowed, as Sarala Das’s words carry across the courtyard into the evening.

dialogue.text: Manuscripts of his work began to circulate, copied by scribes, treasured in local shrines and homes. The epic voice of Odia spread without royal armies, leaf by leaf.

i18n.hi: उनकी रचना की पांडुलिपियाँ चलने लगीं—लेखक बार-बार नकल करते, गाँव के मंदिरों और घरों में संभालकर रखते। ओड़िया की महाकाव्य आवाज़ बिना राजसैनिकों के, पत्ते-पत्ते फैलती गई।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of changing banners atop a fort, with constant village activity below
panels.action: A fort’s silhouette shows banners changing from Ganga to Gajapati emblems over time, while below, the same village road stays busy with carts, cattle, and children playing.

dialogue.text: Dynasties rose and fell in Cuttack and Puri. Yet in the countryside, Sarala’s Mahabharata kept speaking, carrying memories of royal ages through voices that had never entered a court.

i18n.hi: कटक और पुरी में वंश आते-जाते रहे। पर देहात में सरला की महाभारत बोलती रही, राजयुगों की याद उन आवाज़ों में ढोती रही जो कभी दरबार में नहीं पहुँचीं।

panels.shot: archival-feel close-up of a later palm-leaf copy of Sarala Mahabharata in a museum tray
panels.action: In a modern archive room, a gloved hand gently opens an old palm-leaf manuscript, its etched Odia letters darkened by time, resting on foam supports under soft white light.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, institutions like the Odisha State Museum and Utkal University began to collect and digitize such palm leaves, preserving Sarala’s words as historical artifacts and living literature.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतने पर ओडिशा स्टेट म्यूज़ियम और उत्कल विश्वविद्यालय जैसी संस्थाएँ ऐसी ताड़-पत्तियों को जुटाने और डिजिटल करने लगीं, सरला के शब्दों को इतिहास वस्तु और जीवित साहित्य दोनों की तरह बचाने लगीं।

panels.shot: wide shot in a modern classroom where a teacher points to Sarala Das’s name on a board
panels.action: In a contemporary Odia classroom, students sit at wooden desks as a teacher gestures toward a chalkboard where ‘Sarala Das – Adi Kabi’ is written above a timeline of Odia literature.

dialogue.text: Today he is hailed as Adi Kabi, the foundational poet of major Odia vernacular tradition—not the first to speak in Odia, but the one who lifted it into a vast epic form.

i18n.hi: आज उन्हें आदि कवि कहा जाता है—बड़ी ओड़िया लोक-साहित्य परंपरा के आधार कवि; ओड़िया में बोलने वाले पहले नहीं, पर वो शख्स जिसने इसे विराट महाकाव्य रूप में उठा दिया।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Sarala Das’s eyes in lamplight, thoughtful and steady
panels.action: Sarala Das’s face is lit by the small flame of his lamp, deep-set eyes calm and reflective as he looks up from his writing toward the unseen listeners of the future.

dialogue.text: Empires, temples, and titles shift with time, but the vernacular lines Sarala carved kept the memory of an age alive in the hearts of its people, long after the crowns had changed.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य, मंदिर और उपाधियाँ समय के साथ बदलती हैं, पर सरला की गढ़ी लोक-पंक्तियाँ एक युग की याद लोगों के दिलों में ज़िंदा रखती हैं, बहुत बाद तक, जब मुकुट बदल चुके होते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Sarala Das Gives Odia an Epic Voice
title_i18n.hi: सरला दास ने ओड़िया को महाकाव्य की आवाज़ दी

subtitle_i18n.en: When Empires Fall, Words Rise: Sarala Das and the Odia Mahabharata
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब साम्राज्य गिरते हैं, शब्द उठते हैं: सरला दास और ओड़िया महाभारत
